relevance_note: Case report of two children with germline TNFAIP3 variants and A20 haploinsufficiency ("we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20"), with an individual-level literature table of previously published TNFAIP3 patients with HLH/MAS.
method_note: Read the full text, Table 1, Table 2, Table 3 and the reference list; every quote was copied verbatim from the Markdown and re-checked against it. Table 3 is a literature table: its four data rows were read with the 'Author' cell copied into source_reference_in_review (D-23), the 'Number' column read as a bare-number index ('Table 3 #1' and 'Table 3 #2' for the two published patients; rows 3 and 4 are this paper's own Patient one and Patient two, which keep their own labels). The three Zhang et al. 2021 patients described in the Discussion (ref [25]) each have individual-level features and got rows labelled 'ref [25] patient' 1-3. Scope decisions: relatives were included only when the paper gives an individual-level fact about them - the healthy older sister of Patient one and the two parents of Patient two (tested, homozygous wild type; sex not stated); the parents of Patient one appear only collectively (consent, travel, reluctance about etanercept) with no individual-level fact, so they got no rows. Labels: the paper's own headings 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' were used, although Table 3 prints the same people as 'Our patient N. 1' and 'Our patient N. 2'. Contradictions found: (1) for the Li et al. patient the Table 3 cell prints 'c.C259T' while the text prints 'c.259C > T' for the same person - the table form was used in the variant row; (2) for Patient one the text says 'He had normal ESR, CRP, and procalcitonin levels' while Table 1 lists ESR 11 (range 0-10) and CRP 6 (range <6) - the explicit text statement was taken and the tension is noted here; (3) the paper says the HLH criteria were met for Patient one but also says 'it might be suggested that all five HLH criteria were not met in the first patient' and suggests the name HLH/MAS. Age at diagnosis for Patient one was recorded as the age at the genetic (WES) diagnosis, '2 years and 4 months'; HLH was diagnosed at presentation (4 months), recorded as age at onset. No stacked cells (values separated by ' / ') occur in this paper; Table 1 and Table 2 are single-patient laboratory tables with parameter rows, so no positional reading was needed. Variant fields follow D-29: Patient one's zygosity is not stated for him and was not inferred from the haploinsufficiency wording; Table 3 #2's inheritance is not recorded as de novo because no parental testing is reported for that published patient; variant class was not derived from HGVS strings, so it is 'not reported' for Patient one, Table 3 #1 and Table 3 #2 (missense is stated only for Patient two). 'probably deleterious' for Patient two comes from the SIFT/PolyPhen-2 sentence, the closest thing to an authors' classification the paper prints. Genomic coordinates: the text prints the cytogenetic band 6q23.3 for Patient two, which is neither coordinates nor a g. description, so genomic_coordinates_as_stated is null. Normal and negative findings (D-27): Patient one's normal echocardiography and Patient two's normal CSF analysis are written as the paper words them and exclude nothing more specific than what they name; Patient two's 'The skin appeared normal' was taken as excluding the skin-lesion checklist item. The exclusions of oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis and (for Patient one) skin lesions rest on the group statement 'Our patients did not have any symptoms of Behcet’s-like or other autoimmune disorders in the first presentation and subsequent follow-ups'. Boolean fields with no possible quote (is_proband, cites_prior_report_of_same_patients) are false with span null. No script was used; the file was written by hand and its spans re-checked against the paper.
